reasoning_content:
The seaweedfs repo is returning 404, which suggests the GitHub API is rate-limiting or has access restrictions — the rabbitmq repo worked fine, so this might be specific to that repository or a rate limit issue. The "Not Found" error is puzzling since chrislusf/seaweedfs definitely exists, but the rabbitmq API call succeeded moments before with a 67KB response, so it's not a blanket API outage. Let me try a different approach to figure out what's happening.

I could fetch the latest release directly from the HTML page at github.com/chrislusf/seaweedfs/releases/latest and follow the redirect to get the actual version, or try querying the tags endpoint instead.

action.command: timeout 30 curl -s https://api.github.com/repos/chrislusf/seaweedfs/tags?per_page=5 -o /tmp/tags.json; head -c 400 /tmp/tags.json; echo; echo ===; timeout 30 curl -sIL https://github.com/chrislusf/seaweedfs/releases/latest 2>&1 | grep -iE "^HTTP|location" | head -4
